title: Lights — Conversion of the Main Deck Ceiling and Wall Wash Lighting to Solid State Strips

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Conversion of the main deck ceiling and wall wash lighting to addressable solid state strips in the original cabin layout, removing the fluorescent tube supply problem and adding scene control on the attendant panel.

sections.planning_reason: The fluorescent tube used in the original installation was withdrawn from production under restrictions on mercury content and the remaining stock is forecast to run out during 2024. Tube attributed cabin defects run at eleven per thousand flight hours, the largest single contributor to cabin snag lists, and every operator that has refreshed its cabin has asked for scene control that the fluorescent installation cannot provide.
sections.description: The fluorescent tubes and their ballasts are removed and replaced by addressable solid state strips on a new extrusion that clips into the existing lighting channel. The obsolete panel RO886925-91 and the obsolete galley insert D3320009917460 are removed. The partition NY719919-92 is retained and refitted, and bolts LN983579-8C secure the extrusion at each ceiling rib position. The strips are driven from the cabin core system controller that already exists on all aircraft, so no new equipment box is installed.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on ground power and isolate the cabin lighting distribution. Remove the ceiling and wall panels along the run to be converted, working from the forward end. Remove the fluorescent tubes and their ballasts and remove the obsolete panel RO886925-91 and the galley insert D3320009917460. Remove the retained partition NY719919-92 and store it. Clean the lighting channel and install the new extrusion, securing it with bolts LN983579-8C at each ceiling rib position. Clip the solid state strips into the extrusion and connect them in the order given in the accomplishment instructions, keeping the addressing sequence from front to rear. Refit the partition NY719919-92 and the ceiling and wall panels. Energise the cabin and load the lighting addressing into the cabin configuration. Do the lighting installation check of AMM-T-33-20-11-400-002-A and confirm that every scene selection on the attendant panel gives the expected result. Measure and record the cabin lighting current at full brightness. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00213 in the original cabin layout. MSN T00164 and MSN T00188 are excluded, those aircraft having been withdrawn or stored beyond return. Aircraft already converted to the extended premium layout have a different lighting channel geometry and are covered by the conversion Service Bulletin instead.
sections.material_note: Kit K3320-1044-01 covers one main deck. Kit lead time is thirty weeks. Removed tubes are hazardous waste and must be disposed of under the operator's local procedure; they may not be returned to Aeralis.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the exhaustion of the operator's fluorescent tube stock, or at the next cabin refresh, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Addressing sequence corrected at step 7; effectivity extended to MSN T00213
